items.title: Homer (fl. c. 8th century BCE)
items.meta: Archaic Greece · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 2 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Homer

fields.label: Life Dates
fields.value: fl. c. 8th century BCE

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Not English. Dates of composition are traditional, not fixed.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Homer is the traditional poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey. He is placed in the 8th century BCE, probably in Ionia. Old stories call him a blind singer from the Greek east. Many scholars think the two poems had different makers.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Homer in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions match the Iliad and the Odyssey with dates and themes. They also test epic form, oral style, and the Homeric Question (who made the poems).

items.title: Hesiod (fl. c. 700 BCE)
items.meta: Archaic Greece · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Hesiod

fields.label: Life Dates
fields.value: fl. c. 700 BCE

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Poetry / Epic — Works and Days (c. 700 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Hesiod was a Greek poet who lived around 700 BCE. He farmed at Ascra in Boeotia, near Mount Helicon. He says the Muses met him while he kept sheep. His poems teach about the gods, hard work, and justice.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Hesiod in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions separate the Theogony from Works and Days. They also place him beside Homer in Archaic Greece.

items.title: Sappho (c. 630–c. 570 BCE)
items.meta: Archaic Greece · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 1 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Sappho

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Lyric Poetry — Surviving lyric poems / fragments (c. 600 BCE; individual poems vary)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Sappho was a Greek lyric poet from the island of Lesbos. Reference works place her life near 630 to 570 BCE. Most of her poems survive only as short fragments. Later Greeks praised her as the tenth Muse.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Sappho in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions test the Sapphic stanza, the Hymn to Aphrodite, and poems that survive as fragments.

items.title: Aeschylus (c. 525–456 BCE)
items.meta: Classical Greece (Attic Age) · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 2 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Aeschylus

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Drama — Tragedy — Prometheus Bound (date disputed; commonly c. 460–450 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Aeschylus was the earliest of the three great Athenian writers of tragedy. He was born at Eleusis about 525 BCE. He died at Gela, in Sicily, in 456 or 455 BCE. He fought at Marathon and at Salamis, and only seven plays under his name survive complete.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET tests Aeschylus in Unit I (Drama). Questions ask which plays form the Oresteia, and they ask the year 458 BCE. They also ask who added the second actor, and they ask about Prometheus Bound.

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Sophocles

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Drama — Tragedy — Oedipus at Colonus (401 BCE; first performed posthumously)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Sophocles was an Athenian writer of tragedy (serious plays about suffering). He was born at Colonus, near Athens, about 496 BCE. He died in Athens in 406 BCE. Only seven of his many plays survive complete.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET tests Sophocles in Unit I (Drama). Questions ask you to order Ajax, Antigone, Oedipus Rex, and Oedipus at Colonus by year. They also ask about the third actor and tragic irony.

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Euripides

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Drama — Tragedy — Iphigenia in Aulis (c. 405 BCE; posthumous)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Euripides was the youngest of the three great Athenian writers of tragedy. Ancient tradition puts his birth about 480 BCE, near the time of Salamis. He died in 406 BCE, in Macedonia, as a guest of King Archelaus. Nineteen plays under his name survive, more than for Aeschylus or Sophocles.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET tests Euripides in Unit I (Drama). Questions ask the years of Medea, Hippolytus, and The Trojan Women. They also ask which plays were staged after he died.

items.title: Pindar (c. 518–c. 438 BCE)
items.meta: Archaic Greece · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 1 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Pindar

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Lyric Poetry — Epinician Odes (c. 498–446 BCE; individual odes vary)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Pindar was the leading Greek poet of choral victory songs. He was born near Thebes about 518 BCE. He died about 438 BCE, probably at Argos. His epinician odes praise winners at the great Greek games.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Pindar in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions test the epinician ode and the triad of strophe, antistrophe, and epode.

items.title: Plato (c. 428–348 BCE)
items.meta: Classical Greece (Attic Age) · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 14 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Plato

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Philosophy / Prose — Symposium (c. 385–370 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Plato was a Greek philosopher in Classical Athens. He was born about 428 BCE and died about 348 BCE. Socrates was his teacher, and Aristotle was his student. He founded the Academy, a school in Athens.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: Unit 8 (Literary Criticism) tests his attack on poetry. Questions ask about mimesis (imitation) in Republic Book 10. They also ask about Ion, the Symposium, and the Phaedrus. Unit 4 (Non Fictional Prose) may ask students to order the dialogues.

items.title: Herodotus (c. 484–c. 425 BCE)
items.meta: Classical Greece (Attic Age) · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Herodotus

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: History / Prose — Histories (c. 440 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Herodotus was a Greek historian from Halicarnassus. He was born about 484 BCE and died about 425 BCE. Cicero later called him the Father of History. His Histories tell how Greece fought the Persian Empire.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET treats this history as Unit 4 prose. Questions ask why he is called the Father of History, and which wars he records.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Thucydides was an Athenian historian and general. He was born about 460 BCE and died about 400 BCE. He wrote the History of the Peloponnesian War. The narrative breaks off in 411 BCE and was left unfinished.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET

items.title: Aristophanes (c. 446–c. 386 BCE)
items.meta: Classical Greece (Attic Age) · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 4 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Aristophanes

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Drama — Comedy — The Clouds (423 BCE; surviving text is revised)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Aristophanes was the great Athenian writer of Old Comedy (the wild, political comedy of the fifth century). He was born about 446 BCE. He died about 386 BCE. Eleven of his plays survive almost complete, and he mocked war, demagogues (popular leaders), and new ideas.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET tests Aristophanes in Unit I (Drama). Questions ask the years of The Clouds, Lysistrata, and The Frogs. They also ask whom he mocks, and what Old Comedy is.

items.title: Aristotle (384–322 BCE)
items.meta: Classical Greece (Attic Age) · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 9 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Aristotle

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Philosophy / Prose — Nicomachean Ethics (c. 340 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Aristotle was a Greek philosopher and scientist. He was born in Stagira in 384 BCE and died in Chalcis in 322 BCE. He studied at Plato's Academy for about twenty years. In 335 BCE he returned to Athens and founded the Lyceum.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: Unit 8 (Literary Criticism) is built on the Poetics and the Rhetoric. Questions define catharsis, hamartia, peripeteia, and anagnorisis. They also ask for the six parts of tragedy. Unit 4 (Non Fictional Prose) may test the Ethics and the Politics.

items.meta: Hellenistic / Alexandrian Greece · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Theocritus

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Poetry / Epic / Criticism — Idylls (c. 270 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Theocritus was a Greek poet from Syracuse in Sicily. He was born about 300 BCE and died after 260 BCE. He created pastoral poetry, poems about shepherds and country song. His Idylls later shaped Virgil and the English pastoral elegy.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Theocritus in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions test him as the founder of pastoral poetry and of the pastoral elegy.

items.title: Plautus (c. 254–184 BCE)
items.meta: Roman Republic · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Plautus

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Drama — Comedy — The Menaechmi (c. 200–190 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Plautus was the leading comic playwright of the Roman Republic. He was born in Sarsina about 254 and died in 184. He turned Greek New Comedy into loud, musical Latin farce. About 21 of his plays still survive.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Plautus in Unit 1 (Drama) as a source of later comedy. Questions ask which play gave Shakespeare The Comedy of Errors. They also ask the meaning of miles gloriosus, the braggart soldier.

fields.value: Callimachus

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Poetry / Epic / Criticism — Epigrams (3rd century BCE; individual dates vary)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Callimachus was a Greek poet and scholar from Cyrene. He lived about 310 to 240 BCE and worked in Alexandria. He compiled the Pinakes, a large catalogue, at the Library of Alexandria. He preferred short, learned poems to long epic.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Callimachus in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions test the Hymns, the Epigrams, and his rejection of long epic.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Apollonius of Rhodes was a Greek epic poet and scholar. He was born about 295 BCE and worked in the third century BCE. He headed the Library of Alexandria for a time. His Argonautica tells how Jason sought the Golden Fleece.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET

fields.value: Terence

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Drama — Comedy — The Brothers (160 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Terence was a Roman comic playwright of the Republic. Reports place his birth in North Africa about 195 or about 185. He was brought to Rome as a slave, then educated and freed. He produced six plays from 166 to 160 and died in 159.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Terence in Unit 1 (Drama) with Roman comedy. Questions ask the order of Andria, The Eunuch, and The Brothers. They also ask how his prologues and double plots differ from Plautus.

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Prose / Rhetoric — De Republica (54–51 BCE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Marcus Tullius Cicero was a Roman statesman, lawyer, and writer. He was born at Arpinum in 106 BCE and killed at Formiae in 43 BCE. As consul in 63 BCE, he stopped the plot of Catiline. Mark Antony had him killed, and his head and hands were shown in Rome.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Cicero in Unit VIII, Literary Criticism. Questions match De Oratore, De Republica, Brutus, and De Officiis with their years. They also ask what learning the ideal orator must have.

fields.value: Virgil was a Roman poet of the Augustan age. He was born near Mantua in 70 BCE and died at Brundisium in 19 BCE. His Latin name was Publius Vergilius Maro. He wrote the Eclogues, the Georgics, and the Aeneid.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Horace was a Roman lyric poet of the age of Augustus. He was born in Venusia in 65 BCE and died in 8 BCE. He fought for Brutus, then won the friendship of Maecenas. Virgil helped bring him to that powerful patron.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: Unit 2 (Poetry) tests the dates of the Odes and the Satires. Unit 8 (Literary Criticism) tests the Ars Poetica. Questions ask for ut pictura poesis, dulce et utile, and in medias res. They also ask what decorum and purple prose mean.

items.title: Lucretius (c. 99–c. 55 BCE)
items.meta: Roman Republic · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Lucretius

fields.label: Life Dates
fields.value: c. 99–c. 55 BCE

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Poetry — De Rerum Natura (c. 50 BCE; unfinished at death)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Titus Lucretius Carus was a Roman poet and Epicurean thinker. Epicurean means he followed Epicurus, who taught that atoms make the world. He lived about 99 to 55 BCE, though ancient notes disagree on the exact years. His one long poem tries to free readers from fear of the gods and of death.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Lucretius in Unit II, Poetry. Questions identify De Rerum Natura, its six books, and its Epicurean teaching. They also ask why the fear of death is called empty.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Six books of atoms and no fear of death, known to Cicero by 54 BCE. | Poetry — De Rerum Natura (c. 50 BCE; unfinished at death)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Gaius Valerius Catullus was a Roman lyric poet from Verona. He was born about 84 BCE and died about 54 BCE. He belonged to the neoteric poets (new poets who liked short, polished verse). Many of his poems speak of love and anger for a woman he calls Lesbia.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Catullus in Unit II, Poetry. Questions identify the Carmina, the Lesbia lyrics, and the name neoteric or new poet. They also ask for the famous short lines on love and hate.

fields.value: Epic / Poetry — Heroides (c. 25–16 BCE; later additions disputed)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Ovid was a Roman poet born at Sulmo in 43 BCE. His Latin name was Publius Ovidius Naso. Augustus exiled him to Tomis in 8 CE. He died there in 17 or 18 CE.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Ovid in Unit 2 (Poetry). Questions date the Amores, the Ars Amatoria, and the Metamorphoses. They also ask why Augustus exiled him.

fields.value: Drama — Tragedy — Agamemnon (c. 1–65 CE; exact date uncertain)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Lucius Annaeus Seneca was a Roman Stoic (a teacher of calm duty), statesman, and playwright. He was born in Corduba, in Spain, about 4 BCE. He tutored Nero and advised him after Nero became emperor in 54 CE. Nero ordered Seneca to kill himself in 65 CE.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Seneca in Unit I, Drama. Questions identify his tragedies and their Greek sources. They also ask how Thyestes shaped later revenge tragedy.

items.title: Juvenal (c. 55–c. 127 CE)
items.meta: Roman Imperial (Silver Age) · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Juvenal

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Satire / Poetry — Satires (c. 100–127 CE; books published over time)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Decimus Junius Juvenalis was the fiercest Roman satirist (a poet who attacks vice). He was born at Aquinum about 55 CE. Little of his life is certain, and he probably died in or after 127 CE. His sixteen Satires attack greed, cruelty, and the corrupt life of Rome.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Juvenal in Unit II, Poetry. Questions ask for Juvenalian satire, bread and circuses, and a sound mind in a sound body. They also place the Satires in the early 2nd century CE.

items.title: Martial (c. 40–c. 104 CE)
items.meta: Roman Imperial (Silver Age) · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Martial

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Satire / Poetry — Epigrams (c. 86–102 CE; books published over time)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Marcus Valerius Martialis was a Roman poet from Bilbilis, in Spain. He was born about 40 CE and died about 104 CE. He lived in Rome for many years, then returned to Spain near the end of his life. He perfected the Latin epigram, a very short poem with a sharp ending.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Martial in Unit II, Poetry. Questions identify the Epigrams, the years 80 to 102 CE, and the short poem with a final twist.

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Plutarch

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: History / Prose — Moralia (1st–2nd century CE; collection assembled over tim)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Plutarch was a Greek biographer and moral essayist from Chaeronea. He was born about 46 CE and died after 119 CE. He wrote the Parallel Lives and the Moralia. Sir Thomas North's 1579 English Lives became a source for Shakespeare.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Plutarch in Unit 4 prose. Questions test the Parallel Lives, North's 1579 translation, and Shakespeare's Roman plays.

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Marcus Fabius Quintilianus was a Roman teacher of rhetoric (persuasive public speech). He was born in Calagurris, in Spain, about 35 CE. Under Vespasian he became the first Latin rhetoric teacher paid by the state. He died in Rome about 100 CE.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Quintilian in Unit VIII, Literary Criticism. Questions ask for the Institutio Oratoria, its date near 95 CE, and the good man who speaks well.

fields.value: Longinus is the usual name for the author of On the Sublime. The real name is unknown. Some scholars say Pseudo-Longinus. The treatise is usually dated to the 1st century CE.

fields.value: Unit 8 (Literary Criticism) tests On the Sublime. Questions ask for the five sources of sublimity. They also ask who translated the work into French in 1674. Students must not place the author in the 3rd century only.

items.title: Tertullian (c. 155–c. 220 CE)
items.meta: Late Antiquity & Patristic Transition · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Tertullian

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Christian Apologetic Writing — Christian apologetic works (c. 197–220 CE; individual works vary)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Tertullian was an early Christian writer from Carthage in North Africa. He was born about 155 and was still writing after 220. He is the first major Christian author to write in Latin. He later joined the Montanists (a strict prophetic group) and then formed his own group.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET can ask Tertullian with early Christian Latin prose, not with English poetry. Questions ask the date of the Apologeticus and its famous short sentences. They also ask that he later became a Montanist.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: St. Augustine

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Christian Prose / Autobiography — The City of God (413–426 CE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Augustine of Hippo was a North African bishop and Latin Christian writer. He was born in Tagaste in 354 and died in Hippo in 430. He taught rhetoric (the art of persuasive speech) before he became a priest. He became bishop of Hippo in 396 and served until his death.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Augustine in Unit 4 (nonfictional prose) and in early criticism. Questions ask the dates of Confessions and The City of God. They also ask what the two cities mean and that The City of God has 22 books.

items.title: Jerome (c. 382–405 CE; work over several decades)

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Biblical Scholarship — Latin Vulgate Bible — translation/revision (c. 382–405 CE; work over several decades)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Jerome was a Latin priest, monk, and translator of the Bible. He was born at Stridon about 347 and died in Bethlehem in 420. Pope Damasus made him a secretary in Rome in 382. He later directed a monastery in Bethlehem and revised the Latin Bible.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Jerome in Unit 4 (nonfictional prose) for the Latin Vulgate. Questions ask who commissioned the work and when the Hebrew Old Testament was finished. They also ask what the name Vulgate means.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Jerome's Latin Bible: Damasus asks in 382, Gospels about 383, Hebrew Old Testament about 405. | Biblical Scholarship — Latin Vulgate Bible — translation/revision (c. 382–405 CE; work over several decades)

items.title: Boethius (c. 477–524 CE)
items.meta: Late Antiquity & Patristic Transition · Ancient Greek & Roman Classics · 0 PYQs

fields.label: Writer Name
fields.value: Boethius

fields.label: L1 One-Line Flash Anchor
fields.value: Philosophical Prose / Transition — The Consolation of Philosophy (c. 523–524 CE)

fields.label: 2-Minute Simple Biography
fields.value: Boethius was a Roman senator and Christian philosopher. Reference works place his birth about 475 to 477. King Theodoric imprisoned him on a charge of treason. He was executed in 524, after writing The Consolation of Philosophy in prison.

fields.label: Why Important for UGC NET
fields.value: UGC NET asks Boethius in Unit 4 (nonfictional prose) as a bridge into medieval literature. Questions ask where the Consolation was written and who speaks. They also ask which later English writers translated it.

fields.label: Memory Tip & Exam Traps
fields.value: Prison book of 524: five books, Lady Philosophy, wheel of fortune, translated by Alfred, Chaucer, and Elizabeth I. | Philosophical Prose / Transition — The Consolation of Philosophy (c. 523–524 CE)
